reviewType: Read-only interaction review of final task-delegation catch-up with device client readiness
verdict: No merge interaction blocker identified in the reviewed scope
interactionsReviewed: Task assignment uses unified_tasks.project_id and the existing integer projects.id anchor. TaskBoard receives stringified numeric project IDs from its existing server projection and passes numeric scope to assignment controls; it does not reinterpret the device program UUID as an integer.

Device/regional project creation still establishes projects.regulatory_program_id through the canonical transactional anchor; existing authoring-source task resolution still uses that bridge. Incoming assignment changes neither project/program identity nor device product types.

Task assignment reads current organization membership, task/project/workspace and recipient access; assignment changes only assignee/provenance fields with an atomic governed audit record. It does not grant project access, document-review approval or signing rights.

Incoming named and automatic assignment routes share current admission and the request-pinned database connection. RequestConnectable.connect delegates to the same requestPgClient used for admission, mutation and audit; no shared-pool transaction escape was found in this interaction.

Assignment controls retire account/workspace/task changes, require a fresh roster/CAS token and reconcile unknown write outcomes before retry; these controls remain independent of regional preparation-only submission actions.

Incoming CSS is scoped to TaskBoard assignment selectors and existing design tokens; it does not override project or wizard selectors. The existing generated ramp remains owned by its canonical generator.
All fifteen production sources from the prior device/Vault interaction freeze retain their hashes in the release freeze; no source overlap or device behavior change was introduced by task catch-up.
